<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?><!--suppress NavigationFile -->
<navigation xmlns:android="http://schemas.android.com/apk/res/android"
    xmlns:app="http://schemas.android.com/apk/res-auto"
    xmlns:tools="http://schemas.android.com/tools"
    android:id="@+id/nav_graph_personalid"
    app:startDestination="@id/personalid_phone_fragment">

    <fragment
        android:id="@+id/personalid_biometric_config"
        android:name="org.commcare.fragments.personalId.PersonalIdBiometricConfigFragment"
        android:label="fragment_personalid_biometric_config"
        tools:layout="@layout/screen_personalid_verify">
        <action
            android:id="@+id/action_personalid_biometric_config_to_personalid_otp_page"
            app:destination="@id/personalid_otp_page"
            app:popUpTo="@id/personalid_biometric_config" />
        <action
            android:id="@+id/action_personalid_biometric_config_to_personalid_message"
            app:destination="@id/personalid_message_display"
            app:popUpTo="@id/personalid_biometric_config" />
        <action
            android:id="@+id/action_personalid_biometric_config_to_personalid_name"
            app:destination="@id/personalid_name"
            app:popUpTo="@id/personalid_biometric_config" />
    </fragment>

    <fragment
        android:id="@+id/personalid_otp_page"
        android:name="org.commcare.fragments.personalId.PersonalIdPhoneVerificationFragment"
        android:label="fragment_personalid_phone_verify"
        tools:layout="@layout/screen_personalid_phone_verify">
        <action
            android:id="@+id/action_personalid_otp_page_to_personalid_message"
            app:destination="@id/personalid_message_display"
            app:popUpTo="@id/personalid_otp_page" />
        <action
            android:id="@+id/action_personalid_otp_page_to_personalid_name"
            app:destination="@id/personalid_name"
            app:popUpTo="@id/personalid_phone_fragment"/>
    </fragment>

    <dialog
        android:id="@+id/personalid_message_display"
        android:name="org.commcare.fragments.personalId.PersonalIdMessageFragment"
        android:label="fragment_personalid_message"
        tools:layout="@layout/screen_personalid_message">
        <action
            android:id="@+id/action_personalid_message_to_personalid_biometric_config"
            app:destination="@id/personalid_biometric_config"
            app:popUpTo="@id/personalid_message_display" />
        <action
            android:id="@+id/action_personalid_message_to_personalid_backupcode"
            app:destination="@id/personalid_backup_code"
            app:popUpTo="@id/personalid_message_display" />
        <action
            android:id="@+id/action_personalid_message_to_personalid_phone_verify"
            app:destination="@id/personalid_otp_page"
            app:popUpTo="@id/personalid_message_display" />
        <action
            android:id="@+id/action_personalid_message_self"
            app:destination="@id/personalid_message_display"
            app:popUpTo="@id/personalid_phone_fragment"
            app:popUpToInclusive="true"/>
        <argument
            android:name="title"
            app:argType="string" />
        <argument
            android:name="message"
            app:argType="string" />
        <argument
            android:name="callingClass"
            app:argType="integer"
            app:nullable="false" />
        <argument
            android:name="buttonText"
            app:nullable="false"
            app:argType="string" />
        <argument
            android:name="button2Text"
            app:argType="string"
            app:nullable="true" />
        <argument
            android:name="isCancellable"
            android:defaultValue="true"
            app:argType="boolean" />
        <action
            android:id="@+id/action_personalid_message_display_to_personalid_phone_fragment"
            app:destination="@id/personalid_phone_fragment"
            app:popUpTo="@id/personalid_message_display"
            app:popUpToInclusive="true" />
    </dialog>

    <fragment
        android:id="@+id/personalid_backup_code"
        android:name="org.commcare.fragments.personalId.PersonalIdBackupCodeFragment"
        android:label="fragment_personalid_backup_code"
        tools:layout="@layout/fragment_recovery_code">
        <action
            android:id="@+id/action_personalid_backupcode_to_personalid_message"
            app:destination="@id/personalid_message_display"
            app:popUpTo="@id/personalid_backup_code" />
        <action
            android:id="@+id/action_personalid_backupcode_self"
            app:destination="@id/personalid_backup_code"
            app:popUpTo="@id/personalid_backup_code" />
        <action
            android:id="@+id/action_personalid_backupcode_to_personalid_photo_capture"
            app:destination="@id/personalid_photo_capture"
            app:popUpTo="@id/personalid_backup_code" />
        <action
            android:id="@+id/action_personalid_backupcode_to_personalid_email"
            app:destination="@id/personalid_email"
            app:popUpTo="@id/personalid_backup_code" />
        <action
            android:id="@+id/action_personalid_backup_code_to_send_email_otp"
            app:destination="@id/personalid_send_email_otp_fragment" />
    </fragment>

    <fragment
        android:id="@+id/personalid_phone_fragment"
        android:name="org.commcare.fragments.personalId.PersonalIdPhoneFragment"
        android:label="fragment_personalid_phone_fragment"
        tools:layout="@layout/screen_personalid_phoneno">
        <action
            android:id="@+id/action_personalid_phone_fragment_to_personalid_message_display"
            app:destination="@id/personalid_message_display" />
        <action
            android:id="@+id/action_personalid_phone_fragment_to_personalid_biometric_config"
            app:destination="@id/personalid_biometric_config"/>
        <action
            android:id="@+id/action_personalid_phone_fragment_to_personalid_name"
            app:destination="@id/personalid_name" />
        <action
            android:id="@+id/action_personalid_phone_fragment_self"
            app:destination="@id/personalid_phone_fragment" />
    </fragment>

    <fragment
        android:id="@+id/personalid_name"
        android:name="org.commcare.fragments.personalId.PersonalIdNameFragment"
        android:label="personalid_name"
        tools:layout="@layout/screen_personalid_name">
        <action
            android:id="@+id/action_personalid_name_to_personalid_message"
            app:destination="@id/personalid_message_display" />
        <action
            android:id="@+id/action_personalid_name_to_personalid_backup_code"
            app:destination="@id/personalid_backup_code" />
    </fragment>
    <fragment
        android:id="@+id/personalid_photo_capture"
        android:name="org.commcare.fragments.personalId.PersonalIdPhotoCaptureFragment"
        android:label="fragment_personalid_photo_capture"
        tools:layout="@layout/screen_personalid_photo_capture">
        <action
            android:id="@+id/action_personalid_signup_fragment_self"
            app:destination="@id/personalid_photo_capture" />
        <action
            android:id="@+id/action_personalid_photo_capture_to_personalid_message"
            app:destination="@id/personalid_message_display"
            app:popUpTo="@id/personalid_photo_capture" />
    </fragment>

    <fragment
        android:id="@+id/personalid_email"
        android:name="org.commcare.fragments.personalId.PersonalIdEmailFragment"
        android:label="fragment_personalid_email"
        tools:layout="@layout/fragment_personalid_email">
        <argument
            android:name="workflow"
            app:argType="org.commcare.fragments.personalId.EmailWorkFlow" />
        <action
            android:id="@+id/action_personalid_email_to_personalid_photo_capture"
            app:destination="@id/personalid_photo_capture" />
        <action
            android:id="@+id/action_personalid_email_to_personalid_message"
            app:destination="@id/personalid_message_display" />
        <action
            android:id="@+id/action_personalid_email_to_personalid_email_verification"
            app:destination="@id/personalid_email_verification" />
    </fragment>

    <fragment
        android:id="@+id/personalid_send_email_otp_fragment"
        android:name="org.commcare.fragments.personalId.PersonalIdConfigurationSendEmailOtpFragment"
        android:label="@string/personalid_send_email_otp_title">
        <argument
            android:name="email"
            app:argType="string" />
        <argument
            android:name="masked"
            app:argType="boolean"
            android:defaultValue="true" />
        <argument
            android:name="workflow"
            app:argType="org.commcare.fragments.personalId.EmailWorkFlow" />
        <action
            android:id="@+id/action_personalid_send_email_otp_to_email_verification"
            app:destination="@id/personalid_email_verification" />
    </fragment>

    <fragment
        android:id="@+id/personalid_email_verification"
        android:name="org.commcare.fragments.personalId.PersonalIdConfigurationEmailVerificationFragment"
        android:label="fragment_personalid_email_verification"
        tools:layout="@layout/fragment_personalid_email_verification">
        <argument
            android:name="email"
            app:argType="string" />
        <argument
            android:name="workflow"
            app:argType="org.commcare.fragments.personalId.EmailWorkFlow" />
        <argument
            android:name="emailOtpRequestCount"
            app:argType="integer" />
        <action
            android:id="@+id/action_personalid_email_verification_to_personalid_photo_capture"
            app:destination="@id/personalid_photo_capture" />
        <action
            android:id="@+id/action_personalid_email_verification_to_personalid_message"
            app:destination="@id/personalid_message_display" />
        <action
            android:id="@+id/action_personalid_email_verification_to_set_new_backup_code"
            app:destination="@id/personalid_account_config_set_new_backup_code_fragment"
            app:popUpTo="@id/personalid_phone_fragment"
            app:popUpToInclusive="true" />
    </fragment>

    <fragment
        android:id="@+id/personalid_account_config_set_new_backup_code_fragment"
        android:name="org.commcare.fragments.personalId.PersonalIdAccountConfigSetNewBackupCodeFragment"
        android:label="@string/personalid_set_new_backup_code_title">
        <action
            android:id="@+id/action_set_new_backup_code_to_personalid_message"
            app:destination="@id/personalid_message_display"
            app:popUpTo="@id/personalid_phone_fragment"
            app:popUpToInclusive="true" />
    </fragment>
</navigation>

content.text:
I fixed CCCT-2901 with a one-line change in `BasePersonalIdFragment.kt:102`. It compiles and passes the ktlint check, but I haven't tested it on a device, and I haven't committed (you asked me not to commit without your approval).

**Cause:** The "Recover backup code" screen set the app bar title through `supportActionBar.setTitle(...)`. The rest of the screens in the PersonalID flow, including the backup code screen, use `activity.setTitle(...)`. My reading of AppCompat is that once a title is set directly on the action bar, any later `activity.setTitle(...)` call is quietly ignored. So when you press back, the backup code screen tries to restore its title and nothing happens. I worked this out from how AppCompat behaves rather than by stepping through it on a device.

**Fix:** `setTitle(titleResId)` now calls `requireActivity().setTitle(titleResId)`, the same way the other screens do, and I removed the import that was no longer used.

**Profile flow:** the profile version of "Recover backup code" uses the same helper, so it gets the same fix.

**To verify,** follow the ticket's steps: Sign Up/Register → log in with an existing PersonalID account → Forgot backup code → Back. The title should switch back to the backup code screen's title.

content.text:
I added a Robolectric regression test for CCCT-2901 in `PersonalIdBackupCodeFragmentRecoveryTest.kt`. With your fix in place, all 21 tests in the class pass. With the fix stashed, only the new test fails, with the bug from the ticket:

```
expected:<[Confirm Backup C]ode> but was:<[Recover backup c]ode>
```

**What the test does:** it opens the backup code screen in recovery mode using the real nav controller. It taps "Forgot backup code" and checks that the app bar shows "Recover backup code". It then goes back and checks that the app bar shows the confirm-code title again. It checks the app bar's own title rather than `activity.title`, because `activity.title` updates even when the bug is present.

I didn't run ktlint on the test file. Your project rules say not to auto-format existing Kotlin files, and the ktlint task reformats as it checks. Nothing is committed.

When a test checks text shown on screen (titles, labels, app bar), use Espresso APIs (`onView(withText(...))`, scoped with `isDescendantOfA(withId(...))` when needed) instead of writing helper methods that read the text off views or the action bar.

Base directory for this skill: /Users/dimagi/.claude/plugins/cache/dimagi-claude-workflows/dev-utils/1.9.0/skills/create-mobile-pr

# Create GitHub Pull Request

Open a **draft** PR with a JIRA-prefixed title, a description built from the repo's PR template, and `--assignee "@me"`. The user reviews and marks it ready on GitHub. Release/QA notes go in `RELEASES.md`, not the PR body.

Every artifact below has a **recipe** (what it contains) and a **budget** (how long it may be). Fill the recipe with true statements up to the budget, then stop. Write to that shape — do not treat the budget as a target to reach. An artifact that would be empty is omitted entirely, heading and all. **The whole PR body is capped at 120 words** — section bodies, excluding headings and the ticket link. Every section under budget but the body over 120 still fails; drop the least load-bearing section.

**The diff test — apply to every sentence of the PR body.** Before writing a sentence, ask: *could the reviewer learn this by reading the diff?* If yes, delete it. Names of new helpers, params, or values; which file the code lives in; "follows the existing convention"; what a function does mechanically — all visible in the diff, all cut. The PR body exists only for what the code cannot tell the reviewer: why, and what to watch for. `example.md` in this directory is a full worked example of good, terse output.

## Process

### 1. Gather context (parallel)

```
git branch --show-current
git log master..HEAD --oneline
git log master..HEAD          # full messages, fallback for ticket
git diff master...HEAD --stat
git diff master...HEAD
cat .github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md
cat RELEASES.md
```

Fold any notes/context/verification steps the user already gave into the right sections.

### 2. Title

**Recipe:** `TICKET Short Description Of The Change`, derived from the commits and diff (not the branch slug).
**Budget:** ≤72 chars. Title Case every word including short ones (On, To, For, The). Preserve acronym/identifier casing (`SSO`, `URL`, `iOS`, `CCCT-1929`).

Extract `TICKET` (`[A-Z]+-[0-9]+`) from the branch prefix; fall back to commit messages; if still none, ask.
Example: `CCCT-1929 Re-Fetch SSO Token On Invalid Token Error`

### 3. Ask about the author's testing

The Safety story needs what the *author* actually did. If they haven't already said, ask:

> What did you personally do to test this? (ran it on a device, exercised a flow, ran a test suite, reviewed the diff only, etc.)

Wait for the answer. Record it honestly, including "did not test locally." Never invent testing.

### 4. Update RELEASES.md

Find the topmost `## CommCare X.YZ` section. Release Notes and QA Notes are **separate decisions, separate drafts-for-approval, separate commits**. **No JIRA ticket numbers anywhere in RELEASES.md.**

**Release Notes** — go under the `### Release Notes` subsection, in one of `#### What's New`, `#### Important Bug Fixes`, or `#### Internal Release Notes`. Include only if the change is observable by end users or a specific project.
**Recipe:** one bullet stating what changed *from the user's perspective*.
**Budget:** one line per change. No implementation detail.

**QA Notes** — go under the `### QA Notes` subsection. What a tester with only a phone build must manually verify (app UI, settings, forms, Connect, PersonalID, their own test accounts, HQ admin views). A tester has no Android Studio, Logcat, adb, or tests; if a regression is invisible without those, say so and rely on automated coverage instead of writing an unrunnable step.
**Recipe:** one bullet per distinct check, phrased "verify X still works" / "confirm Y behaves as expected." Only non-obvious risks and behavior changes — the tester already knows the happy path.
**Budget:** 1–3 bullets; hard cap 5.

For each: show the user the exact bullet text verbatim and the **release version heading it will go under** (e.g. `## CommCare 2.56`) so they can confirm it is landing in the right release — plus the subsection (`### QA Notes`, or `### Release Notes` → `#### Important Bug Fixes`). Wait for their approval, then commit alone (`Add release notes for TICKET` / `Add QA notes for TICKET`). Do not decide on the user's behalf to skip a note they might want — when in doubt whether a note is warranted, ask.

### 5. PR description

Build from `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md`, replacing every HTML comment with content. **Do not show the description for approval** — it's a draft the user edits on GitHub. Only RELEASES.md needed approval.

**Top of body:** `### [TICKET](https://dimagi.atlassian.net/browse/TICKET)` (display text is just the ticket).

Fill a section only when its recipe has something true to say; otherwise delete that heading and body. Always keep the ticket link and Safety story. **Omit the Labels and Review section.**

- **Safety story** — a neutral risk read in two lists, `**What gives confidence**` and `**Risks to review**`. Rank candidates by how much each one changes the reviewer's read and keep only the top ones, most important first — true is the floor, not the bar. Author actions in **first person** ("I exercised the happy path"); statements about the change in third person. Note a mitigation if there is one; otherwise leave it for the reviewer. `risk-categories.md` lists what to weigh.
  **Budget:** ≤2 items per list, ≤15 words each; ≤55 words total.
- **Technical Summary** — *only* what survives the diff test: why this approach over the obvious alternative, and any non-obvious decision, exclusion, or ordering dependency a reviewer should know before reading. If the diff already speaks for itself, omit the whole section.
  **Budget:** ≤40 words.
- **Product Description** — the user-facing behavior change.
  **Budget:** ≤25 words.
- **Automated test coverage** — what tests were added or changed and what they lock down.
  **Budget:** ≤25 words.

**Verify before building the body:** count the words in each drafted section and recut any that exceeds its budget — drop the lowest-ranked item, or tighten. Then sum them; if the total exceeds 120, cut the least load-bearing section whole.

### 6. Push

```bash
git rev-parse --abbrev-ref --symbolic-full-name @{u}   # upstream?
git push -u origin HEAD    # if none
git push                   # if behind (carries the RELEASES.md commits)
```

### 7. Create the draft PR

```bash
gh pr create --draft \
  --title "TICKET Short Description" \
  --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
<generated description>
EOF
)" \
  --assignee "@me"
```

No `--reviewer` — the user requests reviewers after leaving draft. Capture the printed PR URL for step 8.

### 8. Suggested Review Order comment

Skip if fewer than 2 non-generated files changed.

**Recipe:** the changed files in reading order, each with a short clause of rationale (≤15 words). Order: deleted/replaced code → schema/model/migration → new types/constants → core logic → integration/API → UI → tests (near their code, or first if they document intent) → config/build/cosmetic last. Skip generated files (lock files, compiled output, vendored deps). If the commits already tell a clean story, recommend reading commit-by-commit instead.

```bash
gh pr comment <PR-URL> --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Suggested Review Order

- `path/to/file-1.kt` — reason it comes first
- `path/to/file-2.kt` — reason it comes next
EOF
)"
```

Then output the PR URL.

## Hard rules (mechanical, always)

- Draft PR: `--draft`, `--assignee "@me"`, never `--reviewer`.
- No JIRA ticket numbers in RELEASES.md (release notes or QA notes).
- Each RELEASES.md update is its own commit, and only after the user approves the drafted bullets.
- Omit the template's Labels and Review section.
- Never leave the template's HTML-comment placeholders in the body.
- Every PR body section is at or under its word budget, and the body is ≤120 words.
- Push the branch before `gh pr create`.

## CommCare 2.65

### Release Notes

#### What's New

- The CommCare logo no longer appears on any PersonalID sign-up or account recovery screen.
- PersonalID sign-up, account recovery and profile screens now share consistent headings, text styles, spacing and colors.
- Messaging and Work History now show the sidebar, and opening another sidebar section replaces the current one instead of stacking on top of it.
- After an incorrect email or phone OTP code, PersonalID now shows how many attempts remain before a new code must be requested.
- Opportunities whose visits have no daily limit now show today's visit count without a daily progress bar or "daily limit reached" warning.

#### Important Bug Fixes

- Backing out of the PersonalID phone number screen while the app is contacting the server no longer crashes the app.
- When too many incorrect email or phone OTP codes are entered, the OTP code is now reported as no longer usable and the user is prompted to request a new one, instead of showing a generic error. The wait before a new OTP code can be requested is now shown accurately.
- Fixed an issue where the day and year fields of the date widget used by date questions with a `gregorian` appearance could not be edited with the keyboard in landscape.

#### Internal Release Notes

- Removed the root-menu home screen (the root module grid with a side drawer) and the developer setting that enabled it. Consumer apps now open to the standard home screen.

### QA Notes

- Step through PersonalID sign-up and account recovery and verify the CommCare logo no longer appears, including on the phone number screen.
  - Confirm the name screen's app bar title reads "Name" and not "App Lock".
- On every PersonalID sign-up, recovery and profile screen, including any message sheets that appear, confirm each screen has a heading and no text is oversized or clipped.
- On the PersonalID phone number screen, tap Continue and immediately press back before the request finishes; the app should return to the previous screen without crashing.
- After too many wrong email or phone OTP codes, the field clears, the message explains the OTP code can no longer be used, and Resend is offered straight away.
- Requesting a new OTP code after that should report the remaining wait in minutes or hours, and Resend should stay hidden until it passes.
- A single wrong OTP code still shows the usual incorrect OTP code error, and the option to proceed without email during sign-up is still reachable.
- In the forgot-backup-code recovery flow, running out of attempts keeps the user on the verification screen instead of ending the flow.
- On an app whose menus display as a grid, open a module from the home screen and confirm the grid shows and items open as before.
- On a consumer app, confirm login lands on the standard home screen and pressing back from the root menu returns there.
- Enter wrong email OTP codes during sign-up, profile email edit, and forgot-backup-code recovery, and confirm the error shows the attempts remaining (2, then 1) before the "request a new code" message appears.
- For an invited user receiving the phone OTP by SMS through PersonalID, confirm a wrong code likewise shows the attempts remaining.

app/src/org/commcare/personalId/profile/PersonalIdProfileActivity.kt
package org.commcare.personalId.profile

import android.content.Intent
import android.os.Bundle
import android.widget.Toast
import androidx.navigation.NavOptions
import androidx.navigation.fragment.NavHostFragment
import androidx.navigation.ui.AppBarConfiguration
import androidx.navigation.ui.NavigationUI
import org.commcare.activities.DispatchActivity
import org.commcare.activities.NavigationHostCommCareActivity
import org.commcare.connect.PersonalIdManager
import org.commcare.connect.database.ConnectUserDatabaseUtil
import org.commcare.dalvik.R
import org.commcare.fragments.personalId.EmailWorkFlow
import org.commcare.fragments.personalId.PersonalIdProfileSendEmailOtpFragmentArgs
import org.commcare.google.services.analytics.AnalyticsParamValue
import org.commcare.views.dialogs.CustomProgressDialog

class PersonalIdProfileActivity : NavigationHostCommCareActivity<PersonalIdProfileActivity>() {
    companion object {
        const val EXTRA_PENDING_BACKUP_CODE = "extra_pending_backup_code"
        const val EXTRA_INITIATE_BACKUP_CODE_RECOVERY = "extra_initiate_backup_code_recovery"
    }

    override fun getLayoutResource(): Int = R.layout.activity_personalid_profile

    override fun getHostFragment(): NavHostFragment = supportFragmentManager.findFragmentById(R.id.profile_nav_host) as NavHostFragment

    override fun onPostCreate(savedInstanceState: Bundle?) {
        super.onPostCreate(savedInstanceState)
        val appBarConfiguration = AppBarConfiguration(emptySet())
        NavigationUI.setupActionBarWithNavController(this, navController, appBarConfiguration)
        if (savedInstanceState == null) {
            initiateBackupCodeRecoveryIfRequired()
        }
    }

    private fun initiateBackupCodeRecoveryIfRequired() {
        val isPendingBackupCodeLaunch = intent.getBooleanExtra(EXTRA_PENDING_BACKUP_CODE, false)
        val isInitiateBackupCodeRecovery =
            intent.getBooleanExtra(EXTRA_INITIATE_BACKUP_CODE_RECOVERY, false)
        if (!isInitiateBackupCodeRecovery && !isPendingBackupCodeLaunch) return
        val workflow =
            if (isInitiateBackupCodeRecovery) EmailWorkFlow.FORGOT_BACKUP_CODE_EXISTING_USER else EmailWorkFlow.PENDING_BACKUP_CODE
        val email = ConnectUserDatabaseUtil.getUser().email
        if (email != null) {
            val args =
                PersonalIdProfileSendEmailOtpFragmentArgs
                    .Builder(email, workflow)
                    .setMasked(true)
                    .build()
            val navOptions = NavOptions.Builder()
            if (workflow == EmailWorkFlow.PENDING_BACKUP_CODE) {
                navOptions.setPopUpTo(R.id.personalid_profile_fragment, true)
            }
            navController.navigate(
                R.id.personalid_send_email_otp_fragment,
                args.toBundle(),
                navOptions.build(),
            )
        } else {
            if (workflow == EmailWorkFlow.PENDING_BACKUP_CODE) {
                throw IllegalStateException("EXTRA_PENDING_BACKUP_CODE launched but user has no email")
            }
            showAddEmailToast()
        }
    }

    override fun shouldShowBreadcrumbBar(): Boolean = false

    override fun generateProgressDialog(taskId: Int): CustomProgressDialog =
        CustomProgressDialog.newInstance(null, getString(R.string.please_wait), taskId)

    fun forgetPersonalIdAccount() {
        PersonalIdManager
            .getInstance()
            .forgetUser(AnalyticsParamValue.PERSONAL_ID_FORGOT_USER_PROFILE_PAGE)
        val intent =
            Intent(this, DispatchActivity::class.java)
                .addFlags(Intent.FLAG_ACTIVITY_CLEAR_TASK or Intent.FLAG_ACTIVITY_NEW_TASK)
        startActivity(intent)
        finish()
    }

    fun showAddEmailToast() {
        Toast

package org.commcare.personalId.profile

import android.content.Intent
import android.os.Bundle
import android.widget.Toast
import androidx.navigation.NavOptions
import androidx.navigation.fragment.NavHostFragment
import androidx.navigation.ui.AppBarConfiguration
import androidx.navigation.ui.NavigationUI
import org.commcare.activities.DispatchActivity
import org.commcare.activities.NavigationHostCommCareActivity
import org.commcare.connect.PersonalIdManager
import org.commcare.connect.database.ConnectUserDatabaseUtil
import org.commcare.dalvik.R
import org.commcare.fragments.personalId.EmailWorkFlow
import org.commcare.fragments.personalId.PersonalIdProfileSendEmailOtpFragmentArgs
import org.commcare.google.services.analytics.AnalyticsParamValue
import org.commcare.views.dialogs.CustomProgressDialog

class PersonalIdProfileActivity : NavigationHostCommCareActivity<PersonalIdProfileActivity>() {
    companion object {
        const val EXTRA_PENDING_BACKUP_CODE = "extra_pending_backup_code"
        const val EXTRA_INITIATE_BACKUP_CODE_RECOVERY = "extra_initiate_backup_code_recovery"
    }

    override fun getLayoutResource(): Int = R.layout.activity_personalid_profile

    override fun getHostFragment(): NavHostFragment = supportFragmentManager.findFragmentById(R.id.profile_nav_host) as NavHostFragment

    override fun onPostCreate(savedInstanceState: Bundle?) {
        super.onPostCreate(savedInstanceState)
        val appBarConfiguration = AppBarConfiguration(emptySet())
        NavigationUI.setupActionBarWithNavController(this, navController, appBarConfiguration)
        if (savedInstanceState == null) {
            initiateBackupCodeRecoveryIfRequired()
        }
    }

    private fun initiateBackupCodeRecoveryIfRequired() {
        val isPendingBackupCodeLaunch = intent.getBooleanExtra(EXTRA_PENDING_BACKUP_CODE, false)
        val isInitiateBackupCodeRecovery =
            intent.getBooleanExtra(EXTRA_INITIATE_BACKUP_CODE_RECOVERY, false)
        if (!isInitiateBackupCodeRecovery && !isPendingBackupCodeLaunch) return
        val workflow =
            if (isInitiateBackupCodeRecovery) EmailWorkFlow.FORGOT_BACKUP_CODE_EXISTING_USER else EmailWorkFlow.PENDING_BACKUP_CODE
        val email = ConnectUserDatabaseUtil.getUser().email
        if (email != null) {
            val args =
                PersonalIdProfileSendEmailOtpFragmentArgs
                    .Builder(email, workflow)
                    .setMasked(true)
                    .build()
            val navOptions = NavOptions.Builder()
            if (workflow == EmailWorkFlow.PENDING_BACKUP_CODE) {
                navOptions.setPopUpTo(R.id.personalid_profile_fragment, true)
            }
            navController.navigate(
                R.id.personalid_send_email_otp_fragment,
                args.toBundle(),
                navOptions.build(),
            )
        } else {
            if (workflow == EmailWorkFlow.PENDING_BACKUP_CODE) {
                throw IllegalStateException("EXTRA_PENDING_BACKUP_CODE launched but user has no email")
            }
            showAddEmailToast()
        }
    }

    override fun shouldShowBreadcrumbBar(): Boolean = false

    override fun generateProgressDialog(taskId: Int): CustomProgressDialog =
        CustomProgressDialog.newInstance(null, getString(R.string.please_wait), taskId)

    fun forgetPersonalIdAccount() {
        PersonalIdManager
            .getInstance()
            .forgetUser(AnalyticsParamValue.PERSONAL_ID_FORGOT_USER_PROFILE_PAGE)
        val intent =
            Intent(this, DispatchActivity::class.java)
                .addFlags(Intent.FLAG_ACTIVITY_CLEAR_TASK or Intent.FLAG_ACTIVITY_NEW_TASK)
        startActivity(intent)
        finish()
    }

    fun showAddEmailToast() {
        Toast
            .makeText(
                this,
                R.string.personalid_profile_add_email_toast,
                Toast.LENGTH_LONG,
            ).show()
    }
}

        assertEquals(R.id.personalid_send_email_otp_fragment, navController.currentDestination!!.id)

            activity.supportActionBar?.title,

content.text:
You were right: the PR broke the "Recover backup code" title in the profile flow. I've fixed it locally and the PersonalID tests now pass, but nothing is committed or pushed yet.

**Why it broke:** the profile screens get their titles from the nav graph labels, and that system ignores `Activity.setTitle`. The profile "Recover backup code" screen has no label, so it relied on the direct action bar call my PR removed.

**Existing tests:** one profile test was already failing on the PR: `send email otp screen title is Set Backup Code in pending backup code flow` showed "Profile" instead of "Set Backup Code". No test covered the "Recover backup code" title, so I added `send email otp screen title is Recover backup code in forgot backup code flow` to `PersonalIdProfileActivityTest.kt`. It checks the toolbar text with Espresso.

**New fix:**
- `BasePersonalIdFragment.setTitle` is back to its original code, so the profile flow works as before.
- `PersonalIdActivity` (sign-up/recovery only) now copies every `Activity.setTitle` call to the toolbar. This fixes CCCT-2901 for the backup code screen and any other screen in that flow that sets its title the same way.

**Test results:**

| Code version | Result |
|---|---|
| New fix | All 328 PersonalID tests pass |
| Version currently in the PR | Both profile title tests fail |
| Without the `PersonalIdActivity` change | The CCCT-2901 back-navigation test fails |

The PR's Technical Summary and its risk note describe the old approach, so they're now out of date. Should I commit this as a follow-up commit, push it, and update the PR description?

message.content: what's the difference here between activity.setTitle vs getSupportActionBar.setTitle ? Why can't we use one in both flows?

content.text:
They both change the toolbar title, but AppCompat ranks the two calls differently, and that ranking caused this bug.

**`activity.setTitle(...)`** changes the activity's own title. AppCompat copies it to the toolbar only if nothing has set the toolbar title directly yet. It works as a fallback title.

**`supportActionBar.setTitle(...)`** writes straight to the toolbar and marks the title as set. From then on, `activity.setTitle(...)` still changes the activity title, but the toolbar ignores it. That's what CCCT-2901 showed: the send-OTP screen set the toolbar directly, and on back the backup code screen's `activity.title = ...` did nothing.

The details of that marker come from my reading of how AppCompat works. The tests confirm the behaviour in both directions.

**Why each flow needs a different call today:**
- **Profile flow (`PersonalIdProfileActivity`):** `NavigationUI.setupActionBarWithNavController` calls `supportActionBar.setTitle(label)` on every screen change. After the first screen, `activity.setTitle` can't reach the toolbar in this activity. The send-OTP screen picks its title in code based on the workflow and has no label, so it has to use `supportActionBar.setTitle`.
- **Sign-up/recovery flow (`PersonalIdActivity`):** about nine screens (phone, name, app lock, photo, email, both verification screens, backup code) use `activity.setTitle`. That works only until some screen sets the toolbar directly. The send-OTP base fragment, shared by both flows, was that screen.

**Could we use one call everywhere?**
- **Everything on `activity.setTitle`:** not workable while the profile flow uses `NavigationUI`, because `NavigationUI` always sets the toolbar directly.
- **Everything on `supportActionBar.setTitle`:** workable. That means moving those ~9 screens to the `setTitle` helper in `BasePersonalIdFragment`. The `onTitleChanged` override would then be unnecessary. It's a larger change, and a few of those screens (email and phone verification) are also used in the profile flow. There the fragment's title would replace the nav-graph label. Those strings appear to be the same today, but that needs checking.

**Why I put the fix in the activity:** the `onTitleChanged` override is one change in one place, and it keeps working if a future sign-up screen uses either call. Moving every screen to `supportActionBar.setTitle` is the more consistent long-term option. If you want that instead, I can make the change, drop the override, and rerun the PersonalID tests.

back from Recover backup code
→ toolbar shows Confirm Backup Code"] T2["PersonalIdProfileActivityTest
forgot backup code flow
→ toolbar shows Recover backup code"] T3["PersonalIdProfileActivityTest (existing)
pending backup code flow
→ toolbar shows Set Backup Code"] T1 -->|fails without override| G1["guards sign-up fix"] T2 -->|fails with first attempt| G2["guards profile flow"] T3 -->|fails with first attempt| G2 ``` | Code version | Result | |---|---| | Final fix | All 328 PersonalID tests pass | | First attempt (helper → `activity.setTitle`) | Both profile title tests fail | | No `onTitleChanged` override | Back-navigation test fails | ## 8. content.text:
I wrote the root cause analysis (RCA) to `docs/superpowers/rca/CCCT-2901-rca.md`. I put it under `docs/superpowers/` so it stays untracked and out of the PR, like the other docs there.

It uses Mermaid flowcharts and sequence diagrams, which GitHub and Android Studio render. Its sections are:
1. **Symptom:** the back-navigation title bug from the ticket.
2. **Title rules:** how AppCompat handles `activity.setTitle` versus `supportActionBar.setTitle`.
3. **Who calls what:** which screens use which call, in the sign-up/recovery flow and the profile flow.
4. **Root cause:** the order of title calls in the sign-up flow that left the wrong title showing.
5. **First fix attempt:** why it broke the profile flow, and the two tests that caught it.
6. **Final fix:** the `onTitleChanged` override in `PersonalIdActivity`.
7. **Test coverage:** what each test guards, plus a table of results for each code version.
8. **Alternative considered:** moving every screen to `supportActionBar.setTitle`, and what that would cost.

The text is cut to labels inside the diagrams, plus the results table in section 7.

content.text:
I think Android Studio's Markdown preview needs Mermaid support turned on before it will draw the diagrams. The file itself should be fine: GitHub renders Mermaid without any setup.

**Turn it on in Android Studio:**
1. Open **Settings → Languages & Frameworks → Markdown**.
2. Under **Markdown Extensions**, tick **Mermaid**. If it asks, click **Install** or **Download**, then **Apply**.
3. If there's no Mermaid option, install the **Mermaid** plugin from **Settings → Plugins → Marketplace** and restart Android Studio. Newer versions moved Mermaid support into that separate plugin.
4. Reopen the preview for `CCCT-2901-rca.md`.

If you'd rather not depend on a plugin, I can redraw the diagrams as plain-text (ASCII) charts in code blocks. Those display in any viewer, but they're less tidy, and the sequence diagrams become numbered step lists.

+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+

 Backup code fragment        Send email OTP fragment           Toolbar
         |                              |                          |

+---------------------------------------------+                    |

         |              | |             | | unverified)    | |           |

The section order and the test results table are unchanged. The file is still untracked.

/**
 * Shared Robolectric scaffolding for the Manage Profile fragment tests: boots
 * [PersonalIdProfileActivity] on its start (Profile) destination with a stubbed user record and a
 * mock network server.
 */
abstract class BasePersonalIdProfileTest {
    protected lateinit var activityController: ActivityController<PersonalIdProfileActivity>
    protected lateinit var activity: PersonalIdProfileActivity
    protected lateinit var navHostFragment: NavHostFragment
    protected lateinit var navController: NavController

    protected lateinit var connectUserDatabaseUtilMock: MockedStatic<ConnectUserDatabaseUtil>
    protected lateinit var firebaseAnalyticsUtilMock: MockedStatic<FirebaseAnalyticsUtil>

    protected val mockApiServer = PersonalIdMockApiServer(PersonalIdMockApiServer.CallbackMode.MAIN_LOOPER)
    protected val mockWebServer get() = mockApiServer.server

    protected lateinit var user: ConnectUserRecord

    @Before
    fun setUp() {
        connectUserDatabaseUtilMock = Mockito.mockStatic(ConnectUserDatabaseUtil::class.java)
        user =
            ConnectUserRecord(
                "+11234567890",
                "test-user-id",
                "test-password",
                "Ada Lovelace",
                "",
                null,
                null,
                false,
                "",
                false,
            ).apply {
                email = "ada@example.com"
            }
        connectUserDatabaseUtilMock
            .`when`<ConnectUserRecord> { ConnectUserDatabaseUtil.getUser() }
            .thenReturn(user)
        firebaseAnalyticsUtilMock = Mockito.mockStatic(FirebaseAnalyticsUtil::class.java)
        firebaseAnalyticsUtilMock
            .`when`<NavController.OnDestinationChangedListener> {
                FirebaseAnalyticsUtil.getNavControllerPageChangeLoggingListener()
            }.thenReturn(
                NavController.OnDestinationChangedListener { _: NavController, _: NavDestination, _: Bundle? -> },
            )
        mockApiServer.start()
        launchProfileActivity()
    }

    @After
    fun tearDown() {
        activityController.pause().stop().destroy()
        connectUserDatabaseUtilMock.close()
        firebaseAnalyticsUtilMock.close()
        mockApiServer.shutdown()
    }

    private fun launchProfileActivity() {
        activityController = Robolectric.buildActivity(PersonalIdProfileActivity::class.java)
        activity =
            activityController
                .create()
                .postCreate(null)
                .start()
                .resume()
                .get()

        navHostFragment =
            activity.supportFragmentManager
                .findFragmentById(R.id.profile_nav_host) as NavHostFragment
        navController = navHostFragment.navController
    }

    protected fun onUiThread(block: () -> Unit) {
        activity.runOnUiThread { block() }
        ShadowLooper.idleMainLooper()
    }

    protected fun setText(
        field: TextView,
        value: String,
    ) {
        onUiThread { field.text = value }
    }

    @IdRes
    protected fun currentDestinationId(): Int = navController.currentDestination!!.id
}

package org.commcare.fragments.personalId

/**
 * Launch context for the PersonalID email entry / verification screens.
 *
 *  - [REGISTRATION]: brand-new signup.
 *  - [RECOVERY]: existing user recovering their account after validating the backup code.
 *  - [EXISTING_USER]: a logged-in user adding or verifying their email post-registration.
 *  - [FORGOT_BACKUP_CODE_RECOVERY]: account config graph — user forgot backup code, verifying
 *    via email OTP to complete recovery (session token auth). On OTP success, calls
 *    `complete_recovery` then routes to set-new-backup-code.
 *  - [FORGOT_BACKUP_CODE_EXISTING_USER]: profile graph — logged-in user forgot backup code,
 *    verifying via email OTP to be allowed to set a new backup code.
 *  - [PENDING_BACKUP_CODE]: for the pending-backup-code flow — user has no backup code yet.
 */
enum class EmailWorkFlow {
    REGISTRATION,
    RECOVERY,
    EXISTING_USER,
    FORGOT_BACKUP_CODE_RECOVERY,
    FORGOT_BACKUP_CODE_EXISTING_USER,
    PENDING_BACKUP_CODE,
}

 * Launch context for the PersonalID email entry / verification screens.
 *
 *  - [REGISTRATION]: brand-new signup.
 *  - [RECOVERY]: existing user recovering their account after validating the backup code.
 *  - [EXISTING_USER]: a logged-in user adding or verifying their email post-registration.
 *  - [FORGOT_BACKUP_CODE_RECOVERY]: account config graph — user forgot backup code, verifying
 *    via email OTP to complete recovery (session token auth). On OTP success, calls
 *    `complete_recovery` then routes to set-new-backup-code.
 *  - [FORGOT_BACKUP_CODE_EXISTING_USER]: profile graph — logged-in user forgot backup code,
 *    verifying via email OTP to be allowed to set a new backup code.
 *  - [PENDING_BACKUP_CODE]: for the pending-backup-code flow — user has no backup code yet.
 */
enum class EmailWorkFlow {
    REGISTRATION,
    RECOVERY,
    EXISTING_USER,
    FORGOT_BACKUP_CODE_RECOVERY,
    FORGOT_BACKUP_CODE_EXISTING_USER,
    PENDING_BACKUP_CODE,
}

content.text:
I added toolbar-title tests for every screen in both nav graphs. Each test checks the title when a screen opens and again after pressing Back. All 334 PersonalID tests pass. Nothing is committed or pushed yet.

**New files:**
- `PersonalIdActivityToolbarTitleTest.kt` covers the sign-up/recovery graph: 10 screens and 14 Back cases.
- `PersonalIdProfileActivityToolbarTitleTest.kt` covers the profile graph: 9 screens (the send-OTP screen in all three workflows) and 12 Back cases.
- `NavGraphTitleTestSupport.kt` holds the shared Espresso title check and the code that reads each graph's actions.

content.text:
Yes, I believe it would work. If every screen in the sign-up flow called `supportActionBar.setTitle(x)`, the lock would stop mattering. That's because each screen would write the toolbar title directly, and none would rely on the `activity.setTitle` fallback. I haven't run this variant; the new title tests would confirm it either way.

**Why it would hold up on Back:** a screen only gets its title back if it sets it again when its view is rebuilt. Every screen's title call already runs during view creation (`onCreateView`, or the photo screen's `setUpUi()`). Back rebuilds the view, so the title would be set again.

**What it would change:**
- **Edits:** about 7 call sites move from `activity.setTitle` / `activity.title =` to the `setTitle()` helper in `BasePersonalIdFragment`. They are in the phone, name, app-lock, photo, email and email/phone-verification screens, plus `setUpInitialState` in `BasePersonalIdBackupCodeFragment`. Then the `onTitleChanged` override can be removed.
- **Shared screens:** these 3 also run in the profile flow, where `NavigationUI` sets titles from nav-graph labels:
  - email verification
  - phone verification
  - backup code (including "Set New Backup Code")

  With direct calls, their code would override the label. Today their strings match their labels: "Verify Email", the verify-phone title, "Confirm Backup Code" and "Set New Backup Code". So nothing visible changes, but the code becomes the source of truth for those titles.

**Trade-off:**

| | `onTitleChanged` override (current) | `supportActionBar.setTitle` everywhere |
|---|---|---|
| Size of change | One method in `PersonalIdActivity` | ~7 call sites |
| Future screen uses `activity.setTitle` | Still works | Breaks again. The new title tests would catch it, but only if the screen is in a nav graph. |
| Consistency | Two ways to set a title remain | One way across both flows |
| Effect on profile flow | None | Shared screens' code overrides their nav-graph labels (same strings today) |

The override is the smaller change and tolerates either call. Using `supportActionBar.setTitle` everywhere is cleaner if you want one rule for titles. The new tests guard both approaches, so switching is low risk. Do you want me to switch the PR to that approach?

content.text:
I switched the PR to `supportActionBar.setTitle` everywhere. All 334 PersonalID tests pass, including the new title tests. Nothing is committed or pushed yet.

**Changes:**
- **`PersonalIdActivity`:** the `onTitleChanged` override is removed; the file is back to master.
- **8 call sites:** the phone, name, app-lock, photo, email and email/phone-verification screens, plus `setUpInitialState` in `BasePersonalIdBackupCodeFragment`, now use the `setTitle()` helper in `BasePersonalIdFragment`.
- **The helper:** it now sets both titles: `activity.setTitle(id)`, then `supportActionBar?.setTitle(id)`.

**Why the helper sets both:** using only `supportActionBar!!.setTitle` crashed 6 existing tests with a NullPointerException. When Android recreates the activity, for example after process death or a dark-mode or locale change, fragment views are rebuilt in `onStart`. The toolbar isn't attached until `onPostCreate`, so `supportActionBar` is still null at that point.
- **Already in production:** the existing send-OTP screen already used the same `!!` call, so this PR also removes that crash.
- **Early case:** setting the activity title covers it, because AppCompat applies the activity title when it attaches the toolbar.
- **Activity title:** it stays correct, which two existing tests assert.

**Verification:**
- **Full suite:** all 334 PersonalID tests pass.
- **Catching a regression:** I put one call site (the backup code screen) back to `activity.title = …`. The new tests failed: 7 sign-up title cases, plus the original CCCT-2901 regression test. Then I restored it.

The PR description and the RCA still describe the `onTitleChanged` override. Do you want me to commit this, either as a new commit or folded into the existing one with a force push, and update the PR description and RCA?

content.text:
You're right, the helper doesn't only call `supportActionBar.setTitle` any more. I added `requireActivity().setTitle(titleResId)` as a fallback, and I should have flagged that as a change to the plan rather than slipping it in.

**Why I added it:** with only `supportActionBar!!.setTitle`, 6 existing tests crashed. When Android recreates the activity, for example after process death or a dark-mode or locale change, fragment views are rebuilt during `onStart`. The toolbar isn't attached until `onPostCreate`, so `supportActionBar` is still null when the title is set.

**Options:**

| Option | On recreation | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| A. `supportActionBar?.setTitle` only | No crash, but the title is skipped. The toolbar shows the activity's default title (in the failing tests, the app name "CommCare Debug") until you navigate. | Wrong title after a restore. Two existing tests that assert `activity.title` need rewriting to check the toolbar. |
| B. Current helper: `activity.setTitle`, then `supportActionBar?.setTitle` | AppCompat applies the activity title when it attaches the toolbar, so the title is correct. | Two title calls in the helper, which isn't what we set out to do. |
| C. `supportActionBar.setTitle` only, but set titles in `onResume` | `onResume` runs after `onPostCreate`, so the action bar exists. | Moves the 8 call sites out of `onCreateView`. For the backup code screen, the title is chosen in `setUpView()`, so the chosen title would need storing. Larger diff. |

I recommend B. It's the smallest change that's correct both on Back and after recreation, and the second call is only there because `supportActionBar` can be null at that moment. If you want strictly `supportActionBar.setTitle` only, C does that properly. A leaves the wrong title after a restore.

content.text:
That was the first fix, and it broke the profile flow. The tests showed it: with only `activity.setTitle`, 8 profile cases failed, including the existing "Set Backup Code" test.

**Why:**
- **Sign-up flow (`PersonalIdActivity`):** it would work. If nothing ever calls `supportActionBar.setTitle`, the toolbar is never locked, and every `activity.setTitle` reaches it, including on Back.
- **Profile flow (`PersonalIdProfileActivity`):** `NavigationUI` calls `supportActionBar.setTitle(label)` on every navigation, so the toolbar is locked from the first screen. After that, `activity.setTitle` is ignored there. Most profile screens don't notice because their nav-graph label is the title. The send-OTP screen has no label because its title depends on the workflow, so it shows the previous screen's title. That's the regression you found.

**Making it work:** the profile send-OTP screen would need its title from the nav graph instead of code. The label could be an argument placeholder, `android:label="{title}"`, with the right title passed in from each place that opens the screen. That adds an argument and touches 4 or more callers. It also leaves a rule that's easy to break: never call `supportActionBar.setTitle` in `PersonalIdActivity`.

So `activity.setTitle` alone is only correct if no code ever sets the toolbar title directly. `NavigationUI` in the profile flow always does. I'd still go with B, which sets both titles and is in the working tree now.

message.content: "NavigationUI calls supportActionBar.setTitle(label) on every navigation", is this Android code or code on app side ?

content.text:
Both. The behaviour is in the AndroidX Navigation library, but the app opts into it.

- **Library (AndroidX):** `androidx.navigation.ui.NavigationUI`. When you hook it up to an action bar, it adds a listener to the `NavController`. On every destination change, that listener calls `actionBar.setTitle(label)` using the destination's `android:label`. If a destination has no label, it leaves the title alone. That's why the send-OTP screen, which has no label, showed the previous screen's title.
- **App:** `PersonalIdProfileActivity.onPostCreate` turns it on with:
  ```kotlin
  NavigationUI.setupActionBarWithNavController(this, navController, AppBarConfiguration(emptySet()))
  ```
  `PersonalIdActivity` doesn't make this call, which is why the two flows behave differently.

**What this means for the `activity.setTitle`-only idea:** the lock in the profile flow comes from an app-level choice. If the profile activity stopped calling `setupActionBarWithNavController` and its screens set their own titles, `activity.setTitle` alone would work in both flows. But that call also manages the toolbar's Up arrow for the profile flow, so removing it means re-checking Up/Back behaviour on every profile screen and moving every label-based title into code. That's a much larger change than this ticket.

- **Technical Summary:** it now describes the current approach.         MockAndroidKeyStoreProvider.registerProvider()
        Settings.Global.putInt(context.contentResolver, Settings.Global.AIRPLANE_MODE_ON, 1)

            Manifest.permission.ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION,
            Manifest.permission.ACCESS_COARSE_LOCATION,

        host.setUp()

    }

    fun tearDown() {
        host.tearDown()
        MockAndroidKeyStoreProvider.deregisterProvider()
    }

            token = "test_session_token",

            bootActivityAndSeedSession(sessionData)
            activityController.visible()
            ShadowLooper.idleMainLooper()
            booted = true

        override fun tearDown() {
            destroyActivity()
            super.tearDown()

content.text:
I moved the shared test logic into a new base class, `BaseNavGraphToolbarTitleTest`, and both title tests now extend it. They pass. I also re-checked that they still catch both bugs:
- **Backup code screen back on `activity.title`:** 7 sign-up cases fail.
- **Helper without the direct toolbar call:** 8 profile cases fail.

Nothing is committed yet.

**The base class** (`app/unit-tests/src/org/commcare/personalId/BaseNavGraphToolbarTitleTest.kt`) holds:
- the three tests: every screen has an expected title, each title shows on arrival, and Back restores the title;
- the navigation and per-case error-collection helpers.

Each subclass provides the nav graph, its table of screens, optional extra arrival cases, the current activity and nav controller, and `launch()`.

**The subclasses** now contain only setup and their tables of screens. The two classes went from 199 lines to 83 between them, offset by the 112-line base.
- **Profile test:** it keeps its own mocks and its own `launch()`.
- **Sign-up test:** it still needs `BasePersonalIdConfigurationTest`'s setup (integrity-token mock, mock server, session seeding). Kotlin allows only one base class, so a small private `Host` class inside the test extends `BasePersonalIdConfigurationTest` and exposes `launch`, `setUp` and `tearDown`. The alternative was moving that setup out of `BasePersonalIdConfigurationTest`, which about 20 other tests use.

ktlint changed nothing in the new base file. I didn't run it on the two edited test files, because you had already reformatted them.

### [CCCT-2901](https://dimagi.atlassian.net/browse/CCCT-2901)

## Product Description
Bug Fix: Pressing back from "Recover backup code" now restores the previous screen's app bar title.

## Technical Summary

We were using 2 different expressions to set title `supportActionBar.setTitle` and `Activity.setTitle` in different fragments which created a conflict between pages as  ``supportActionBar.setTitle` locks the title which can't later be updated by the `activity.title` call. The solution I ended up choosing here is to set the title with both calls to  ``supportActionBar.setTitle` and `activity.title` so that even if the title is locked , `activity.title`  call can update it. 


Another solution I tried here is to only set the `supportActionBar.setTitle` but this caused the title to gets skipped during activity recreation as the  supportActionBar is `null` while fragments are rebuilt, this is also the reason that the helper also makes the supportActionBar.setTitle call null safe. 

## Safety Assurance

### Safety story
**What gives confidence**
- Toolbar-title tests cover every screen in both nav graphs, on arrival and after Back.
- I reproduced the ticket steps on a device; the title now updates on back.


[CCCT-2901]: https://dimagi.atlassian.net/browse/CCCT-2901?REDACTED

content.text:
No, I was wrong. You've rewritten the description since my last edit, and it no longer mentions 334 or any test count, so nothing needs changing for the removed tests.

Reading your version, two things look off:

1. **First paragraph, cause and effect reversed:** "set the title with both calls … so that even if the title is locked, `activity.title` call can update it". It's the other way round: once the title is locked, `activity.title` can't update the toolbar. The `supportActionBar?.setTitle` call is what gets past the lock. The `activity.title` call is there for activity recreation, when `supportActionBar` is still null and AppCompat applies the activity title once the toolbar is attached. Your second paragraph already describes that.
2. **Formatting:** ``` ``supportActionBar.setTitle` ``` appears twice with an extra backtick, which will render wrongly on GitHub.

Want me to fix those two points in the description?
